limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).
Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.
DeckCheck's Threat Index is shown in `context` and never scored.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.
rank over n=5 decks; no significance claim

findings.note: validate-rating OK; rating --json matches components, withheld, code_score, bracket, limits exactly.

58 claims the measured parts oversell how often the engine switches on, but the speed component already prices assembly: benchmark kill_by_turn_8 is 0.565 (n=10000), kill_by_turn_10 0.905, never_kills_rate 0.095. The cited 73%/58%/10% are drawn-by-turn-6 shares of card groups, not kill rates; the 10% storm-payoff-plus-ritual group is not needed for the 90.5% kill by T10 (combos.json: 0 infinite lines). Deducting for assembly again on top of speed double-counts it. The only non-measured evidence is two losses on an older list (log 002 decklist_sha c8651652... differs from current 5cf3...).

'median over games that assemble': goldfish.py takes the median over games with a kill_turn (never-kill 9.5% excluded), so true in spirit though it says killed, not assembled. Resilience 37.5 is indeed the lowest component. The two log characterisations (001 bad keep, 002 'The engine never assembled.') match the logs.

judgment.argument: The measured parts miss assembly. No table record on this list (two games, both on the old one), no survey, no Forge run on it, and the new cards are still arriving, so no game has been played with it. I am filling in for that. What they already carry, and I do not deduct again: resilience (answer capacity, scored lowest) and the sweeper gap in construction. Speed and mana are priced from the goldfish. What they undersell is the design: the commander is cast by turn six in 95% of games and a passing stack backs the Crimson Wisps line. What they oversell is how often the engine switches on. An early token maker is drawn in 73% of games, Zada is online with a cantrip in 58%, and storm payoff plus ritual in 10%. The kill turn is a median over games that assemble. The record points the same way: the pilot's second loss reads "The engine never assembled." and the first was a bad keep. Those are two games on the old list, not a verdict, and Forge's 6/100 (95% CI 3% to 15%) is on that older list and is not a power read until the harness work is done. So 58: the assembly figures and the losses pull under the measured score, the design and commander reliability keep it close.
